blockdesc-stovepipe: Joins up automatically, and round corners diagonally (one block up or down and over, or round the corner of a wall). Run it from a Kitchen Range, Kiln Oven, Crucible Furnace, Potbelly Stove, Smoker, Charcoal Retort or clay oven to a Clay Brick Chimney (draft bonus), up through a roof (to a chimney above it, or into a brick chimney top of its own if you don't place one), or out through a wall to open air, so a closed room doesn't fill with smoke. Optional - stoves work without it. To run a pipe through a wall, hold a wrench in your offhand and a block (a chiselled block keeps its carved shape) in your main hand, and use it on the pipe to cover it. Wrench in the offhand and an empty hand takes the cover off.
stovepipe-handbook-text: A fire makes smoke by its fuel: wood is normal, charcoal, coke and coal give very little, peat, dung and hay a lot. In a closed room, smoke that can't get out collects under the ceiling and builds downward, so a tall room takes longer to fill. You only choke once it is down to your head - crouch to get under it - and a fire smoulders and works 40% slower once the smoke reaches it. Everything that burns smokes, not just stoves: torches (in a holder, on a wall or in your hand), lamps, lanterns and candles a little, and a forge, bloomery, pit kiln, charcoal pit, burning coal pile or open fire a lot - a forge or other fire with a chimney straight above it doesn't smoke the room. A few torches only haze the ceiling, but a lot of them in a small sealed room build up. Fire from lightning or a burning house is the worst of all: a room on fire fills in seconds, and even outdoors, standing close to a big fire chokes you - get upwind, crouch, or move away. Thatch, hay, leaves, chiselled gaps and doors let some smoke out wherever it has reached them, so a thatched hut with one small fire stays only hazy. Vent a fire by putting a chimney straight above it (up to 8 blocks), running stovepipes from it to a chimney, or running stovepipes out of the room into open air. A chimney also gives a draft that makes the fire work up to 25% faster - more when it's windy, less in rain or still air. Each chimney can only carry so much smoke: one block carries about one and a half fires, and each block you stack on top adds half a fire more (up to five). Run too many fires into one chimney and the draft drops and the extra smoke backs up into the room - build it taller or add another. Spare chimney capacity also draws smoke out of the room.
blockdesc-kitchenrange-copper-*: Cooks on 1 plate, a tiny bit faster than a firepit. Takes a pot of food or a single food item on each plate. It has no oven. Burns firewood, charcoal or coal.
blockdesc-kilnoven-copper-*: Fires 2 raw clay items at once in about 12 in-game hours (6 with charcoal): tool moulds, ingot moulds, pots, crucibles and other pottery. Needs fuel that burns at 650°C or more for moulds. Melting metal is done in the Crucible Furnace.
blockdesc-kitchenrange-tinbronze-*: Cooks on 2 plates, a bit faster than a firepit. Takes a pot of food or a single food item on each plate. Its oven bakes 1 item at a time. Burns firewood, charcoal or coal.
blockdesc-kilnoven-tinbronze-*: Fires 3 raw clay items at once in about 10 in-game hours (5 with charcoal): tool moulds, ingot moulds, pots, crucibles and other pottery. Needs fuel that burns at 650°C or more for moulds. Melting metal is done in the Crucible Furnace.
blockdesc-kitchenrange-iron-*: Cooks on 3 plates, faster than a firepit. Takes a pot of food or a single food item on each plate. Its oven bakes 2 items at a time. Burns firewood, charcoal or coal.
blockdesc-kilnoven-iron-*: Fires 4 raw clay items at once in about 8 in-game hours (4 with charcoal): tool moulds, ingot moulds, pots, crucibles and other pottery. Needs fuel that burns at 650°C or more for moulds. Melting metal is done in the Crucible Furnace.
blockdesc-kitchenrange-steel-*: Cooks on 4 plates, the fastest of all. Takes a pot of food or a single food item on each plate. Its oven bakes 3 items at a time. Burns firewood, charcoal or coal.
blockdesc-kilnoven-steel-*: Fires 5 raw clay items at once in about 6 in-game hours (3 with charcoal): tool moulds, ingot moulds, pots, crucibles and other pottery. Needs fuel that burns at 650°C or more for moulds. Melting metal is done in the Crucible Furnace.

blockdesc-cruciblefurnace-copper-*: Melts metal in a crucible. Reaches 1100°C: enough for copper and every bronze, with charcoal or coal. Put a fired crucible in the furnace and its ingredients beside it, like a firepit. Once the metal is molten, set a mould in front of the spout and hold right-click on the crank on the gearbox to tip the furnace and pour. Or run an axle into the gearbox (on the left as you face the spout) and flip the clutch lever on top: whenever the axle turns, it pours on its own into any empty mould in front, then waits for the next one. Pours into any mould the game lets you pour into, including other mods' moulds. Use tongs to lift out a hot crucible.
blockdesc-cruciblefurnace-tinbronze-*: Melts metal in a crucible, faster, and holds half as much again. Runs 10% hotter than its fuel, up to 1475°C: with coke it melts nickel (1325°C). Put a fired crucible in the furnace and its ingredients beside it, like a firepit. Once the metal is molten, set a mould in front of the spout and hold right-click on the crank on the gearbox to tip the furnace and pour. Or run an axle into the gearbox (on the left as you face the spout) and flip the clutch lever on top: whenever the axle turns, it pours on its own into any empty mould in front, then waits for the next one. Pours into any mould the game lets you pour into, including other mods' moulds. Use tongs to lift out a hot crucible.
blockdesc-cruciblefurnace-iron-*: Melts metal in a crucible, faster, and holds twice as much. Runs 25% hotter than its fuel, up to 1700°C: with coke it reaches iron (1482°C) and titanium (1668°C) heat. Put a fired crucible in the furnace and its ingredients beside it, like a firepit. Once the metal is molten, set a mould in front of the spout and hold right-click on the crank on the gearbox to tip the furnace and pour. Or run an axle into the gearbox (on the left as you face the spout) and flip the clutch lever on top: whenever the axle turns, it pours on its own into any empty mould in front, then waits for the next one. Pours into any mould the game lets you pour into, including other mods' moulds. Use tongs to lift out a hot crucible.
blockdesc-cruciblefurnace-steel-*: Melts metal in a crucible, fastest, and holds two and a half times as much. Runs 45% hotter than its fuel, up to 1950°C: with coke it reaches chromium (1907°C) heat. Put a fired crucible in the furnace and its ingredients beside it, like a firepit. Once the metal is molten, set a mould in front of the spout and hold right-click on the crank on the gearbox to tip the furnace and pour. Or run an axle into the gearbox (on the left as you face the spout) and flip the clutch lever on top: whenever the axle turns, it pours on its own into any empty mould in front, then waits for the next one. Pours into any mould the game lets you pour into, including other mods' moulds. Use tongs to lift out a hot crucible.
blockdesc-retort-copper-*: Burns firewood and logs without air to make charcoal, and black or brown coal to make coke. Needs fuel to heat it. Joins to stovepipes and chimneys like a stove, and makes a lot more smoke than other stoves, so vent it well when indoors.
blockdesc-retort-tinbronze-*: Burns firewood and logs without air to make charcoal, and black or brown coal to make coke. Needs fuel to heat it. Joins to stovepipes and chimneys like a stove, and makes a lot more smoke than other stoves, so vent it well when indoors.

blockdesc-potbellystove-*: A small cast-iron stove for one pot. Cooks like a firepit, keeps a room warm and burns its fuel slowly. Works with Rustic Cookery's roasting dish.
blockdesc-smoker-*: A farm smokehouse, two blocks tall. Hang raw or cured meat or fish inside and keep a small wood fire going; it smokes in about a day. Raw red meat, bush meat, poultry and fish fillets become smoked meat, and cured meat becomes cured and smoked meat, which keeps even longer. Smoking doesn't cure meat: cure it with salt in a sealed barrel first if you want cured and smoked. Smoked meat goes in stews and soups like cured meat. With Primitive Survival installed it makes that mod's smoked meat instead, and takes its trussed meat (four pieces at once). Charcoal and coal give little smoke.
